sentences.text: Parvodus represents a genus of extinct hybodont sharks that inhabited the Mesozoic seas.
The specific name honours the Brazilian author Graciliano Ramos, who lived from 1892 to 1953.
Its discovery pushes the known range of Parvodus into Upper Jurassic deposits of South America.
Ribeiro and França formally described Parvodus graciliani.
The type specimens were recovered from the Aliança Formation in Brazil.
Isolated teeth recovered from lake-derived sediments indicate the animal’s feeding apparatus.
These lake deposits were oxygen-rich and supported a varied fauna that included hybodont sharks.
Parvodus graciliani is placed within the order Hybodontiformes and assigned to the family Lonchidiidae.
The species lived during the Late Jurassic period.
